learning_outcomes.text: Know the fundamental principles of automatic control systems used in Mechanical Engineering.
Understand the structure and functionality of control elements: transducers, controllers, actuators.
Know the types of controllers (P, PI, PD, PID) and theoretical and experimental tuning methods.
Understand how to model and simulate dynamic systems using differential equations and transfer functions.
Be able to model and simulate control systems using transfer functions and software tools.
Apply experimental methods for identifying and analyzing the response of controlled systems.
Perform the selection and sizing of equipment for implementing a control structure.
Analyze the behavior of control systems in open-loop and closed-loop.
Demonstrate responsibility in using laboratory equipment and respecting testing procedures.
Be able to elaborate clear technical reports regarding the analysis and control of automatic systems.
Demonstrate autonomy in investigating the dynamic behavior of automatic control systems used in Mechanical Engineering.

syllabus_topics: Introductory problems. Subject of the discipline; connection with other disciplines; Definition of automatic systems in engineering systems (industrial, research, etc.)
Process modeling. First-order differential equation. Second-order differential equation. Transfer functions.
Automatic control structure (SRA). Description. Component elements: Transducers; Actuators; Controller.
Automatic control structure (SRA). Types of controllers - Proportional Controller; Integral Controller; Proportional-Derivative Controller; Proportional-Integral-Derivative Controller.

Tuning techniques for Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller parameters. Theoretical considerations; Experimental tuning methods in open-loop; Experimental tuning methods in closed-loop; Model-based tuning methods; Optimal criteria-based tuning methods.
Occupational safety. Laboratory presentation. Review of Basics of Automatic Systems: Systems; Models; Operational calculus; Transfer Function (TF); Step response h(t).
Bi-positional and tri-positional controllers; Direct action controllers.
assessment_rules: The final grade results from considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. A minimum grade of 5 is required for both the Colloquium and Laboratory activities. Grades are awarded as integers from 1 to 10, with a grade of 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the allocation of associated study credits.
